basis: Inherited platelet dysfunction causes bleeding; bruising and episodic muscle or joint bleeds do not establish common lasting tissue damage.
Defined by thyroid C-cell neoplasia, pheochromocytoma and parathyroid disease; hypertension is a secondary complication and reported in under 30%.
Renal epithelial carcinoma arising in acquired cystic kidneys; no common direct extrarenal involvement established.
Congenital bilateral corneal tumors impair vision; the definition explicitly excludes systemic abnormalities.
Congenital atrioventricular septal defect with left heart obstruction; both defining abnormalities are cardiovascular.
Late infantile vanishing white matter disease is a leukodystrophy causing progressive central nervous system dysfunction.
Bile acid metabolic defect with hepatic disease; encephalopathy/neuropathy and pigmentary retinopathy each frequent (30-79%). Malabsorption does not establish intestinal damage.
Venous valve dysfunction impairs venous return; edema alone is insufficient, and damaging skin ulceration is not common across this umbrella.
Partial color blindness is an impairment of ocular color vision.
Congenital cleft affects the shared laryngeal/tracheal and esophageal partition; recurrent infections are secondary complications.
Inherited high myopia, documented in 5/5 patients; no extraocular disease established.
Diabetic retinal vascular leakage damages the macula; diabetes is the underlying separate disease.
Progressive skeletal muscle degeneration defines this umbrella; cardiac and respiratory involvement vary by subtype and are not established in most patients.
Peripheral demyelinating/axonal neuropathy; distal muscle atrophy and weakness occur in 20/20 patients. Cataracts and neutropenia lack evidence of >=30% frequency.
Renal tubular disease in 6/6; cholestasis and intellectual disability each in 2/6 (~33%). Hypertension is secondary; retinal disease occurs in only 1/6.
Defining optic nerve, pituitary and midline brain abnormalities; cleft palate is annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting gastrointestinal involvement.
Umbrella concept explicitly defined as disease involving the stomach.
Skeletal dysplasia with shortening of the middle and distal limb segments; no other organ involvement established.
Odontogenic epithelial lesion arising within jaw bone, usually the mandible, with local expansion and destructive potential.
Ependymal tumor arising in the central nervous system, usually the cerebral ventricles; listed extracranial tumors are rare separate neoplasms.
Primordial skeletal growth disorder with microcephaly and developmental/intellectual impairment in 2/2. Ectopic kidney in 1/2 does not establish renal dysfunction.
Hereditary peripheral arterial occlusion defines a vascular disease; common lasting injury to other organs is not established.
Beta2-microglobulin deposits predominantly damage joints and bone; carpal tunnel neuropathy is a major manifestation, commonly >=30%. Renal failure is antecedent.
Definition localizes the reactive fibroblastic lesion mainly to deep subcutaneous tissue; the name does not establish muscle disease or an immune mechanism.
Ovarian neoplasms arise in a reproductive organ; hormone-secreting subtypes do not define this broad umbrella.
